question: Software Quality Engineering involves the complete development process mainly to ensure that:

options.A: Testing is done only at the end of the project
options.B: Agreed-upon processes, standards and procedures are being followed

explanation:
Software Quality Engineering covers the whole development process to ensure agreed-
upon processes, standards and procedures are followed, with no cherry picking.

question: Why is it difficult to define software quality?

options.A: Software systems are always small and simple
options.C:
Modern systems interconnect multiple underlying software, with little standardization and a 
varied nature
options.D: Customers do not care about quality

explanation:
Modern systems are interconnections of multiple underlying software, and the lack of 
standardization and varied nature make quality hard to define.

question: In Software Quality Engineering, "cherry picking" of standards:

options.D: Is required by International Organization for Standardization 9126

explanation:
The module states that standards must not be cherry picked; the agreed standards are 
followed as a whole.

question: The stakeholders of software development are divided into:
explanation: Stakeholders are divided into consumers (users and customers) and producers.

question: Which group uses the services acquired by the customer?
explanation:
Users use the services that the customer has acquired; the customer is the one who 
acquires the software and services.

question:
Beyond the expectations of users, the customer (who acquires the software) additionally 
concentrates on:

options.B: The cost of the software solution

explanation:
The customer shares the users' expectations but additionally concentrates on the cost of 
the software solution.

question:
A user expectation that specified functions work correctly over repeated use or over a long period of 
time relates to:
explanation: Performing the specified functions correctly over repeated use or a long period is reliability.

question: What is the biggest concern of producers?

options.A: Fulfilling contractual obligations by producing software that conforms to specifications
options.C: Lowering the price of the software

explanation:
Producers mainly want to meet their contractual obligations by delivering products that 
conform to the specifications.

question: Producers of software solutions include:

options.D:
People involved in development, management, maintenance and service, plus third-party 
products and organizations

explanation:
Producers include people in development, management, maintenance and service, as well 
as third-party products and organizations.

question:
Plug-and-play products developed and tested independently of a software solution are usually 
known as:
explanation:
Off-the-Shelf products are plug-and-play items known as plugins, developed and tested 
independently to provide reusable functionality.

question: Why should proper analysis be done before selecting an Off-the-Shelf product?

options.B: Off-the-Shelf products are tested with the solution
options.C: One solution does not fit all

explanation: One solution does not fit all, so selecting an Off-the-Shelf product needs proper analysis.

question: International Organization for Standardization 9126 is:

options.A:
An international standard for software evaluation with a hierarchical framework for quality 
definition

explanation:
International Organization for Standardization 9126 is the international standard for 
software evaluation and gives a hierarchical framework of quality characteristics.

question:
Which of the following is NOT one of the six top-level quality characteristics of International 
Organization for Standardization 9126 discussed in the module?
explanation:
The six characteristics are functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability and 
portability; security is not among them.

question: The functionality characteristic tells us:

options.A: How easily software can be learned
options.B:
How well software provides and performs the desired functions that satisfy stated or implied 
needs
options.C: How many resources the software uses
options.D: How well software moves between environments

explanation:
Functionality shows how well the software provides and performs the functions that satisfy 
stated or implied needs.

question:
"The capability of software to maintain its level of performance under stated conditions for a 
stated period of time" defines:
explanation:
This is the definition of reliability: maintaining the performance level under stated 
conditions for a stated period.

question: The usability characteristic allows stakeholders to conclude how easily a solution can be:
explanation: Usability tells how easily a solution can be learned, understood and used.

question:
The 2007 switch from keyboard to touch screen, linked to the quote "Machines can be user 
friendly too," illustrates:
explanation: The touch-screen switch made machines easier to use, which is the idea of usability.

question: Efficiency relates the level of software performance to:

options.B: The resources used (disk space, memory, network, and so on)

explanation:
Efficiency relates the level of performance to the resources used, such as disk space, 
memory and network.

question: Which of the following is a subcomponent of maintainability?
explanation:
Analyzability, changeability, testability and stability are the subcomponents of 
maintainability.

question: Maintainability refers to attributes that bear on:

options.A: Moving software to a new operating system
options.B: How easily novices can use the software
options.C: The effort needed to make specified modifications

explanation:
Maintainability concerns the effort needed to make specified modifications, that is, to 
identify and repair faults.

question:
A feature that works in one version of an Operating System but fails in another version of the same 
platform is mainly a concern of:
explanation:
Portability is the ability to transfer software from one environment to another, including 
different Operating System versions.

question: An error is best defined as:

options.B: An incorrect step in a program
options.C: The inability of a program to behave as expected
options.D: A human action that produces an incorrect result

explanation: An error is a human action (a programmer's mistake) that produces an incorrect result.

question: Which of the following is a cause of error according to the module?

options.B: Confusion in understanding the requirements of the software

explanation:
The module lists confusion about requirements, miscalculation and misinterpretation of 
values as causes of errors.

question:
In the Hypertext Preprocessor example, writing if ($Amount=100) instead of if 
($Amount==100) is an example of a:
explanation: Using = (assignment) instead of == (comparison) is a logic mistake, so it is a semantic error.

question: A defect refers to:
explanation:
A defect is a deviation from customer requirement, mostly found after the software is 
shipped.

question: In the online payment example, the debit card option missing in the production software is a:
explanation:
The user expects debit card payments, but the production software lacks them, a deviation 
from requirements, that is, a defect.

question: Bugs are the errors found:

options.B: Before the software is shipped into production

explanation: Bugs are the errors found before the software is shipped into production.

question: The Mariner I (1962) failure was caused by:

options.A: A formula written on paper that was improperly transcribed into computer code

explanation:
A formula written in pencil was wrongly transcribed into code, so the rocket's trajectory 
was miscalculated.

question: A fault is:

options.C: An incorrect step, process or data definition in a computer program

explanation:
A fault is an incorrect step, process or data definition in a program; faults are the result of 
errors.

question:
A program meant to add 5 and 3 uses ans = value1 - value2. The wrong sign is the ___ and the 
subtracted output is the ___.
explanation:
The wrong sign in the code is the fault; the resulting incorrect output (subtraction instead 
of addition) is the failure.

question: According to Laprie, a system failure occurs when:

options.A: A developer makes a syntax mistake
options.D: The delivered service no longer complies with the specification

explanation: A failure is when the delivered service no longer complies with the agreed specification.

question: Defect prevention is a strategy to:

options.C: Identify the root causes of defects and prevent them from recurring
options.D: Increase the size of the code

explanation: Defect prevention identifies the root causes of defects and prevents them from recurring.

question: In the defect filter figure, customer requirements pass through which sequence of filters?

options.D: Requirement → Design and Planning → Coding → Testing

explanation:
The figure filters defects in this order: requirement defects, design and planning defects, 
coding defects, then testing defects.

question: According to the module, which expectation is unrealistic?

options.B: A project or product with a zero bug count

explanation: A zero bug count is unrealistic; even a 99.99% bug-free product is not 100% bug-free.

question: Defect containment mainly aims to:

options.D: Break the causal relation between faults and failures, or reduce the resulting damage

explanation:
Containment breaks the causal relation between faults and failures (tolerating faults) or 
reduces the resulting damage.

question: Simplistically, quality means that a product should:
explanation: The lecture defines quality, in simple terms, as meeting the specification.

question:
A requirements document says only administrators may export a report, while another 
section says every user can export it. Which problem with software specifications does this show?
explanation:
The lecture says software specifications are usually incomplete and often inconsistent; two 
sections that contradict each other are an inconsistency.

question:
Which of the following is NOT a reason why the "meet its specification" view is problematical for 
software?

options.A: There is a tension between customer and developer quality requirements
options.B: Some quality requirements are difficult to specify unambiguously
options.C: Specifications are usually incomplete and often inconsistent
options.D: Software specifications are always perfect and complete

explanation:
The lecture says specifications are usually incomplete and often inconsistent, so "always 
perfect" is false.

question: The lecture says there is a tension between:

options.C: Customer quality requirements and developer quality requirements

explanation:
Customers and developers care about different quality requirements, which creates 
tension.

question:
A product passes every check against its specification, but users cannot apply discount 
codes because the specification never mentioned them. What does this show?

options.A: Customers and developers always want the same qualities
options.C: All quality requirements are easy to specify

explanation:
The product met its specification, but the specification missed a needed feature, which 
shows that specifications are usually incomplete.

question:
A team releases a week early by skipping reviews and then receives many defect reports. 
Which definition of quality did the team put ahead of "doing it right the first time"?
explanation:
Releasing early at the cost of reviews favors speed of delivery over doing it right the first 
time.

question:
An app calculates everything correctly, but users need a manual to find basic features. 
Which listed definition of quality is the app missing?
explanation: An app that works but is hard to use is not a good, usable product.

question: Which emphasis does the course place on software quality?

options.B:
Quantitative assessment of software quality and quality control using software testing 
techniques

explanation:
The course places particular emphasis on quantitative assessment of software quality and 
on quality control using software testing techniques.

question:
A company fixes reported bugs, answers support questions and follows up with customers 
after each release. Which definition of quality does this best match?
explanation:
Support, follow-up and bug fixing after release serve the customer's overall experience, 
which is total customer service and satisfaction.

question: Which option correctly matches each quality type with an example?

options.A:
Functional: the page loads in 1 second; Non-functional: the invoice total is correct; Latent: it 
still works after growth
options.B:
Functional: the invoice total is correct; Non-functional: the page loads in 1 second; Latent: it 
still works well after the customer base doubles
options.C:
Functional: it still works after growth; Non-functional: the invoice total is correct; Latent: the 
page loads in 1 second
options.D:
Functional: the page loads fast; Non-functional: it still works after growth; Latent: the invoice 
total is correct

explanation:
Functional quality is what the software does, non-functional quality is how well it does it, 
and latent quality is how well it will keep doing it in the future.

question: Which grading component carries the highest weight in the course?
explanation: Final Term carries 50%, the largest share of the grading.

question: Software quality assurance consists of a means of:

options.A: Monitoring the software engineering processes and methods used to ensure quality

explanation:
The Quality Engineering slide describes Software Quality Assurance as monitoring the 
processes and methods used to ensure quality.

question:
A manager checks whether the team follows its agreed development methods instead of 
only looking at the finished software. Which activity is this?
explanation:
Software quality assurance monitors the processes and methods used, not just the final 
product.

question:
A customer opens an app and is pleasantly surprised by how much it does beyond what 
was asked. Which definition of quality does this match?
explanation: Exceeding what the customer expected is delighting or pleasing the customer.

question: Which of the following is NOT listed under "Defining Quality"?
explanation:
The slide lists perfection, consistency, eliminating waste and similar items; maximizing 
profit is not among them.

question: Which of the following is a non-functional requirement?

options.A: The login button must authenticate valid users
options.B: The search page must return results within 2 seconds
options.C: The system must email a receipt after purchase
options.D: Users must be able to reset their passwords

explanation:
Non-functional quality is about how well the software does something; a response-time 
limit is a non-functional requirement, while the other options describe what the software does.

question:
An auditor checks that every release followed the company's documented rules before 
approving it. Which definition of quality does this reflect?
explanation:
Checking releases against the organization's documented rules is compliance with policies 
and procedures.

question: What is the combined weight of the Quiz, Assignment and Presentation?
explanation: Quiz 5% + Assignment 5% + Presentation 10% = 20%.

question:
Users complain that a payroll system is slow and often unreliable. Which kind of quality 
requirement is affected?
explanation:
Efficiency and reliability are the customer quality requirements, and slow, unreliable 
behavior affects exactly those.

question:
A development team wants code that is easy to modify and can be reused in later projects. Which 
kind of quality requirement is this?
explanation:
Maintainability and reusability are the developer quality requirements named in the 
lecture.

question:
A banking app behaves the same way on every run and on every release. Which 
definition of quality does this best match?
explanation: Behaving the same way every time and across releases is consistency.

question:
A banking app calculates interest correctly today, but there are signs it will not keep working well 
as its data grows. Which quality type is at risk?
explanation: Latent quality measures how well the software will continue to do its job in the future.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three quality types in Lecture 1?
explanation:
Lecture 1 presents functional, non-functional and latent quality; process quality is 
introduced in Lecture 2.

question:
A shopping app has a working checkout, but checkout takes 40 seconds. Which quality type is 
weak?
explanation:
Non-functional quality compares how well the software does something with how well it 
should; a correct but very slow checkout falls short here.

question:
A password reset feature is supposed to email a reset link but does nothing. Which quality type is 
lacking?
explanation:
Functional quality compares what the software does with what it is supposed to do; a reset 
feature that does nothing fails that test.

question:
Lecture 1 names efficiency and reliability as customer quality requirements. Which pair 
of Module 01 quality characteristics do they correspond to?
explanation:
Efficiency and reliability are two of the six top-level quality characteristics of the ISO 9126 
framework from Module 01.

question:
A team removes defects during development so that no rework is needed after release. Which 
definition of quality does this match?

options.B: Doing it right the first time

explanation: Fixing defects early so that nothing has to be redone matches "doing it right the first time".

question:
A photo app crashes when saving certain images, and it also takes a full minute to open. 
Which two quality types are weak?
explanation:
Crashing when saving means it does not do what it should (functional), and the slow start 
means it does not do it well enough (non-functional).

question: Which statement about quality types in Lecture 1 is TRUE?

options.A: Functional quality measures how fast the software runs
options.B: Non-functional quality measures only whether features exist
options.C: Latent quality measures what the software did in the past
options.D:
Functional quality compares what the software does with what it should do, while non-
functional quality compares how well it does it with how well it should

explanation:
Functional quality is about what the software does, and non-functional quality is about 
how well it does it.

question: Which of the following is NOT a definition of quality listed in Lecture 1?

options.A: Lowest possible price for the customer
options.B: Doing it right the first time

explanation:
The Defining Quality slide does not list the lowest possible price; the other three options 
are on it.

question:
A customer wants the fastest possible response times, while the developers want to 
restructure the code so it is easier to modify and reuse, which will delay delivery. Which Lecture 1 idea 
does this show?

options.B: A tension between customer quality requirements and developer quality requirements

explanation:
Speed is a customer requirement, while modifiability and reusability are developer 
requirements, so the two compete.

question:
A requirement says "the system should be fast." Which problem with quality requirements does 
this show?

options.B: They are the same for every stakeholder
options.C: Some of them are difficult to specify in an unambiguous way

explanation:
A word like "fast" is open to interpretation, which shows that some quality requirements 
are hard to specify unambiguously.

question:
"Delighting or pleasing customers" focuses on ___, while "compliance with policies and 
procedures" focuses on ___.

options.C: The organization's own rules; the customer
options.D: The customer; the organization's own rules

explanation:
Delighting or pleasing customers is customer-focused, while compliance with policies and 
procedures is about following the organization's own rules.

question:
A team removes duplicated work and unnecessary steps from its process. Which definition of 
quality does this match?
explanation: Removing duplicated work and unnecessary steps is eliminating waste.

question:
A student scores full marks in the Mid Terms and the Final Term but zero in everything 
else. What percentage of the course grade did the student earn?
explanation: Mid Terms 30% + Final Term 50% = 80%.

question: Which quality type expresses the degree to which defined processes were followed and completed?
explanation:
Process quality is the degree to which the defined software processes were followed and 
completed.

question: Product quality is determined by:

options.D: The degree to which the developed software meets the defined requirements

explanation:
Software products are the output of processes, and their quality depends on how well they 
meet the defined requirements.

question:
Which quality type addresses the degree to which a product is fit for purpose when exposed to a 
particular context of use?
explanation: Quality in use is about fitness for purpose in a particular context of use.

question: Software processes implement which of the following in an organizational context?
explanation:
The lecture says software processes implement best practices of software engineering in an 
organizational context.

question: Software products are the output of:
explanation:
This is why process quality and product quality are linked: products are the output of 
software processes.

question: How many different views of quality are listed in the lecture?
explanation: The views are transcendental, user, manufacturing, product and value-based.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the different views of quality?
explanation: There is no testing view in the lecture's list.

question: Which of the following is a view of quality listed in the lecture?
explanation: Manufacturing view is one of the five listed views.

question: Which set correctly lists the views of quality?
explanation: The lecture lists transcendental, user, manufacturing, product and value-based views.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard quality model in the lecture?

options.B:
International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission 
9126
options.C: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

explanation:
The Goal-Question-Metric Approach is listed under application or company-specific 
models.

question: Which of the following is a standard quality model?
explanation:
McCall is a standard model, along with International Organization for 
Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission 9126 and the Institute of Electrical and 
Electronics Engineers.

question: Functionality, Usability, Reliability, Performance, Supportability is an example of:

options.C: An application or company-specific quality model

explanation:
Functionality, Usability, Reliability, Performance, Supportability and the Goal-Question-
Metric approach are listed as application or company-specific quality models.

question: The Goal-Question-Metric Approach is classified as:

options.B: An application or company-specific quality model

explanation:
The lecture places Goal-Question-Metric next to Functionality, Usability, Reliability, 
Performance, Supportability under application or company-specific models.

question: Which set lists the standard quality models?

options.B:
McCall, Functionality-Usability-Reliability-Performance-Supportability, Institute of Electrical 
and Electronics Engineers
options.C:
International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission 
9126, Goal-Question-Metric, Functionality-Usability-Reliability-Performance-Supportability
options.D:
McCall, International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical 
Commission 9126, Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers

explanation:
The standard quality models are McCall, International Organization for 
Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission 9126 and the Institute of Electrical and 
Electronics Engineers.

question: Which are the categories of Cost of Quality in the lecture?

options.A: Prevention cost, appraisal cost and failure cost
options.B: Design cost, coding cost and testing cost
options.C: Hardware cost, software cost and people cost
options.D: Fixed cost, variable cost and legal cost

explanation: Cost of quality is split into prevention, appraisal and failure costs.

question: Failure cost is further divided into:
explanation: The lecture shows internal failure cost and external failure cost under failure cost.

question: Which of the following is NOT a cost of quality category listed?
explanation: Only prevention, appraisal and failure costs are listed.

question: Which cost of quality category has internal and external sub-types?
explanation: Failure cost is divided into internal and external failure cost.

question: Quality Assurance deals with:
explanation: Quality Assurance deals with defects found before release and after release.

question: The classification scheme for Quality Assurance has which three parts?

options.C: Defect prevention, defect reduction (detection) and defect containment

explanation:
The scheme is defect prevention, defect reduction (also called defect detection) and defect 
containment.

question:
Software quality assurance is described as all planned and systematic activities implemented 
within the:
explanation:
The definition refers to planned and systematic activities implemented within a quality 
system.

question: According to the Software Quality Assurance definition, the activities are meant to provide:

options.D: Adequate confidence that an entity will fulfill requirements for quality

explanation:
The aim is adequate confidence that the entity will fulfill quality requirements, not a 
guarantee of zero defects.

question: Which of the following is part of defect prevention?
explanation:
Defect prevention includes education and training, process conformance and standards 
enforcement, and tools, technologies and techniques.

question: Which of the following is NOT a defect prevention activity?
explanation: Dynamic testing belongs to defect reduction.

question: Defect reduction includes which activities?
explanation: Defect reduction (detection and removal) consists of static and dynamic testing.

question: Defect reduction is also referred to as:
explanation: The slide labels it defect reduction (defect detection and removal).

question: Defect containment includes:

options.A: Software fault tolerance and fault containment

explanation: Software fault tolerance and fault containment make up defect containment.

question: Process conformance and standards enforcement falls under:
explanation: It is one of the three defect prevention activities.

question: Software fault tolerance belongs to:
explanation: Fault tolerance is listed under defect containment.

question: Which items are listed under Software Review in the Software Quality Assurance topics?

options.A: Formal Technical Reviews and Review Guidelines
options.B: Software Quality Assurance Team and Software Quality Assurance Plan

explanation: Software Review covers Formal Technical Reviews and Review Guidelines.

question: Which set lists the Software Quality Assurance team roles from the lecture?

options.B: Testing Manager, Test Team Lead, Test Analyst, Tester, Independent Test Observer
options.D: Test Lead, Developer, Observer, Planner, Coder

explanation: These five roles are given on the Software Quality Assurance Team slide.

question: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Software Quality Assurance team in the lecture?
explanation: Project Sponsor is not in the Software Quality Assurance team list.

question: Independent Test Observer is listed as:

options.D: A member of the Software Quality Assurance team

explanation: It is the last role on the Software Quality Assurance Team slide.

question: The Software Quality Assurance plan is:

options.B: An outline of quality measures to ensure quality levels within a software development effort

explanation: The plan outlines the quality measures used to ensure quality levels during development.

question:
What does the Software Quality Assurance plan allow, and what happens if quality levels fall 
outside the plan?

options.A:
Actual quality levels are compared with planned levels; management responds as 
documented in the plan

explanation:
The plan compares actual and planned quality levels, and management responds as 
documented when they differ.

question: According to the module, the definition of software quality:

options.B: Is fixed by the International Organization for Standardization only
options.C: May differ among developers, users, clients, managers and software quality engineers

explanation:
Quality is perceived and defined differently by developers, users, clients, managers and 
quality engineers.

question: The definition of quality becomes even more complicated when quality depends upon:

options.A: The circumstances or environment in which the software is used

explanation:
The definition becomes harder when quality depends on the circumstances or environment 
in which the software is used.

question: What does the literature reveal about software?

options.A: It has the lowest failure rate of all products
options.B: It has the highest failure rate in the history of all products
options.C: It fails at the same rate as hardware

explanation:
The module says software has the highest failure rate in the history of all products, causing 
losses of millions of dollars.

question:
In the economics of Software Quality Engineering, everything in the process of software 
development ends up in:
explanation: Everything in software development ends up in the user's satisfaction.

question: The satisfaction of the user depends on:

options.C: The overall behavior of the system

explanation:
User satisfaction depends on the overall behavior of the system, with the software product 
coming first.

question: The behavior of a software product is defined and comprehended through:
explanation:
The behavior of a software product is defined and understood through its features and 
quality.

question: Features and quality of a software product are defined or determined through:
explanation: Features and quality are determined through the requirements.

question: Any behavior-related requirement can only be actualized through:
explanation:
Any behavior-related requirement can only be actualized through code that executes the 
behavior.

question: Which software quality has tangible economic value?
explanation:
Only better-than-average software quality has tangible economic value; low quality brings 
serious economic consequences.

question: In the Function-Quality-Cost discussion, functionality and quality are described as:
explanation:
Functionality and quality compete for the same fixed budget, so they are called natural 
enemies.

question: Projects with open budgets are:

options.A: Very rare, so the budget is usually fixed

explanation:
Open budgets are very rare, so budgets are usually fixed and functionality and quality 
compete for a share.

question: What happens if features are increased in a closed-budget project?

options.D: The budget share for quality decreases

explanation:
More features in a closed budget leave a smaller share of the budget for quality, so quality 
decreases.

question:
In the example, the total budget is Pakistani Rupees 100,000 for 4 features. What is the cost per 
feature?
explanation: 100,000 ÷ 4 features = Pakistani Rupees 25,000 per feature.

question: How is risk defined in the risk analysis approach?

options.A: By its cost and its duration
options.B: By its probability and its impact (potential loss)
options.C: By its source and its location
options.D: By its priority and its owner

explanation:
The module defines risk by its probability and its impact or potential loss; Risk Exposure is 
the product of the two.

question: According to the impact analysis approach, what can people face in the worst case?

options.A: Physical injuries, up to the extent of death
options.B: A slight increase in subscription fees
options.C: A change of software vendor only
options.D: No effect, because the impact is limited to the supplier

explanation:
In the worst case, people are exposed to physical injuries to the extent of death; customers 
may also face a stop in business operations because of a bug.

question: Why does quality often suffer in practice, according to the module?

options.D:
Companies are under pressure to deliver more features, ignoring Quality Assurance and its 
long-term damage

explanation:
Companies are pressed to deliver more features and ignore Quality Assurance, causing 
long-term damage.

question: Putting more money into software quality results in:

options.C: A lower probability of product failure

explanation:
More money for quality means a lower probability of product failure and more immunity to 
threats.

question:
A product has an excellent User Interface but no database firewall. What does the module 
conclude?

options.A: User Interface improvements are more important
options.B:
Adding a firewall to secure the database is more important than cosmetic User Interface 
changes

explanation: Securing the database with a firewall matters more than cosmetic User Interface changes.

question: Which statement about the Yahoo breach is correct?

options.A: It was reported in 2014 and occurred in 2016
options.B: It affected fewer than one million accounts
options.C: It was reported in 2016 but occurred in late 2014, affecting at least half a billion accounts

explanation:
The breach was reported in 2016 but occurred in late 2014, exposing information of at 
least half a billion accounts.

question: After the breach, Verizon and Yahoo revised the sale price to:
explanation:
The module gives the revised offer as $4.48 billion, lower than the original $4.8 
billion price.

question: According to Eppler and Helfert, the costs of missing quality are classified as:
explanation: Eppler and Helfert classify the costs of missing quality as direct and indirect.

question: Direct costs of missing quality are:
explanation: Direct costs are tangible, visible and measurable, and occur immediately after the event.

question: Which of the following are examples of direct cost?

options.A: Loss of reputation and market share

explanation: Financial loss and physical injury are the module's examples of direct cost.

question: Indirect costs of missing quality are:

options.C: Invisible, difficult to calculate, and may appear long after the incident

explanation: Indirect costs are invisible, hard to calculate and can show up long after the incident.

question: Which of the following are examples of indirect cost?

options.D: Loss of market share, reputation and shareholders' trust

explanation: Loss of market share, reputation, shareholders' trust and investment are indirect costs.

question: The Nokia Chief Executive Officer's farewell remark (May 2016) is used as an example of:
explanation: The Nokia remark is the module's example of indirect cost, such as loss of market position.

question: The impact analysis approach is based on which sequence?

options.A: Fix it → Identify problem → Root-cause analysis → Keep going
options.B: Identify problem → Keep going → Fix it → Root-cause analysis
options.C: Root-cause analysis → Identify problem → Fix it → Keep going
options.D: Keep going → Fix it → Identify problem → Root-cause analysis

explanation: The sequence is root-cause analysis, identify the problem, fix it, keep going.

question: In the Yahoo case, what did Yahoo (the supplier) face?

options.A: Loss of trust, financial loss, lawsuits and the cost of investigating the root cause

explanation:
Yahoo faced loss of trust, financial loss, lawsuits and the cost of investigating the root 
cause.

question: Why is the risk analysis approach preferred for evaluating the cost of missing quality?

options.B: The time and place of missing-quality events are difficult to determine

explanation:
Since the time and place of missing-quality events are hard to predict, risk analysis gives a 
better cost evaluation.

question: Risk Exposure is calculated as:
explanation:
Risk Exposure is the product of the risk probability and the potential loss: Risk Exposure = 
Probability × Loss.

question: If the risk probability is 0.2 and the potential loss is Pakistani Rupees 500,000, the Risk Exposure is:
explanation: Risk Exposure = Probability × Loss = 0.2 × 500,000 = Pakistani Rupees 100,000.

question:
Which Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers criticality level involves continuous usage (24 
hours per day), irreversible environmental damage and loss of human lives?
explanation:
Level A (Catastrophic) covers 24-hour continuous usage, irreversible environmental 
damage, loss of human lives and disastrous impact.

question:
Which level involves serious threats to human lives, permanent injury or severe illness, and 
important economic or social impact?
explanation:
Level B (Critical) covers serious threats to human lives, permanent injury or severe illness, 
and important economic or social impact.

question:
Which level involves continuous usage with fixed interruption periods, property damage and minor 
injury or illness?
explanation:
Level C (Marginal) covers continuous usage with fixed interruption periods, property 
damage and minor injury or illness.

question: Which level involves time-to-time usage, low property damage and no risk to human lives?
explanation:
Level D (Negligible) covers time-to-time usage, low property damage and no risk to human 
lives.

question: Regardless of the product, its complexity or size, the purpose of Quality Assurance is to:

options.A: Add as many features as possible
options.B: Reduce defects to a minimum to ensure minimum disruption

explanation:
Whatever the product's size or complexity, Quality Assurance aims to reduce defects to a 
minimum to ensure minimum disruption.

question: According to the document, through standards and best practices, defects:

options.D: Can be reduced to a minimum level but not totally removed

explanation:
Standards and best practices can reduce defects to a minimum, but a product with zero 
bugs is not possible.

question: High-priority or sensitive areas of a product should be:
explanation: High-priority or sensitive areas of the product should be defect-free.

question: The relationship between Quality Assurance and defects is:

options.C: Tied to each other and can never vanish

explanation:
Quality Assurance and defects are always tied together and the relationship can never 
vanish.

question: As a last resort, Quality Assurance ensures that:

options.B: Critical functionality works and defects do not threaten or damage it
options.C: The product is released without testing

explanation:
The last resort is that critical functionality must at least work and defects must not threaten 
or damage it.

question: Which set lists the three categories of the Quality Assurance classification scheme?

options.D: Defect Prevention, Defect Reduction (Detection), Defect Containment

explanation:
The three categories are defect prevention, defect reduction (also called defect detection) 
and defect containment.

question: Defect Prevention (Error Source Removal) is the process of:

options.A: Addressing root causes of defects to prevent their future occurrence
options.B: Executing the product to find bugs

explanation:
Defect prevention (error source removal) addresses root causes so defects do not occur 
again.

question: Defect Reduction (Detection) involves approaches such as:

options.C: Quality Assurance, code reviews, code inspection and design review

explanation:
Defect reduction (detection) works through Quality Assurance, code reviews, code 
inspection and design reviews, to find defects early.

question: Defect Containment measures:

options.B:
The amount of defects Quality Assurance found as a portion of total defects, with the focus 
on reducing escaping defects

explanation:
Containment looks at the defects Quality Assurance found as a portion of the total, with 
the focus on reducing escaping defects.

question: Pre-release defects are also described as:
explanation: Pre-release defects are called dormant defects because they can lie inactive until triggered.

question: Why are pre-release defects dormant?

options.A:
They are triggered only in a specific situation, or sit in a low-priority area with little Quality 
Assurance attention

explanation:
They are triggered only in a specific situation or sit in a low-priority area with little Quality 
Assurance concentration.

question:
The cash register that failed when a customer paid using cash, credit card and a gift voucher 
together illustrates:

options.C: A pre-release (dormant) defect triggered by an untested uncommon situation

explanation:
Paying with cash, card and voucher is uncommon and was not tested, so the dormant 
defect surfaced and froze the system.

question: Pre-release defects found at client sites are usually:

options.B: Mentioned as part of the release notes (and fixed depending on impact)

explanation: Depending on impact they must be fixed, but they are usually part of the release notes.

question: Post-release defects are those that:

options.A: Appear in production or at the customer site

explanation: Post-release defects are those that appear in production or at the customer site.

question: Who pays to fix post-release defects?
explanation: The software supplier company pays out of its own pocket to fix post-release defects.

question: Why do post-release defects cost more to fix?

options.C: The product has multiple installations and the defect must be fixed at every place

explanation: With multiple installations of the product, the fix has to be applied at every place.

question: Besides financial loss, post-release defects negatively impact:

options.B: Company image, trust, reputation and market position

explanation: Company image, trust, reputation and market position are all negatively affected.

question: In the Comma-Separated Values export example, what went wrong at the production site?

options.A: Records went missing after about 500,000 records
options.B: The Comma-Separated Values file could not be created
options.D: The Comma-Separated Values file had extra columns

explanation:
The Comma-Separated Values file was generated at production, but records went missing 
after 500,000 records.

question: How was the Comma-Separated Values problem resolved?

options.D:
By generating a separate Comma-Separated Values file after 500,000 records and merging 
the files into a third file

explanation:
The fix was to create a separate Comma-Separated Values file after 500,000 records and 
merge the two files into a third file.

question: Why was the Comma-Separated Values defect missed during Quality Assurance?

options.A: Quality Assurance did not test the export at all
options.C:
The export was tested with only 30,000 records because the Software Requirements 
Specification mentioned no upper limit

explanation:
Quality Assurance tested with 30,000 records because the Software Requirements 
Specification mentioned no upper limit.

question: Defect prevention helps to:

options.B: Reduce the number of defects and the cost to fix them

explanation:
Defect prevention reduces both the number of defects and the cost of fixing them, and digs 
into their sources.

question: What is the best way to prevent defects?

options.A: Detect them as early as possible, find the source and take corrective actions
options.B: Wait for customers to report them

explanation:
Detect defects as early as possible, find the source and take corrective actions to avoid 
them in future.

question: Why is team education and training important for defect prevention?

options.C: It removes the need for requirements
options.D: Lack of skills or relevant training can lead to defects that could otherwise be prevented

explanation:
People are a critical factor; lack of skills or training can cause defects that could have been 
prevented.

question: Software developers are generally considered:

options.C: Pure technical resources, so domain specialists are hired for some projects

explanation:
Developers are pure technical resources, so some projects hire domain specialists to work 
with analysts and developers.

question: Low domain-specific knowledge can lead to:

options.B: Ambiguity, confusion and demotivation among the team

explanation:
Domain terms vary between domains, so low domain knowledge leads to ambiguity, 
confusion and demotivation.

question: In the property tax example, a domain specialist is needed to:

options.D: Derive the appropriate rates and formula

explanation:
The property tax project needs a domain specialist to derive the appropriate rates and 
formula.

question:
Which is an example of lack of knowledge in Software Development Life Cycle phases that can 
cause defects?

options.A: Lack of knowledge of Requirement Management or Product Integration

explanation:
Lack of knowledge of Requirement Management or Product Integration is a root cause of 
defects.

question: Regarding process knowledge, the document states that:

options.A: Creating a process and implementing it are the same
options.B: Creating a process and on-boarding/implementing it are two different things

explanation:
Creating a process and on-boarding or implementing it are different things, and success 
depends on both.

question: In the change request example, a Project Manager unaware of change management may:

options.C:
Ask developers to write out-of-scope code, delaying in-scope features and causing defects in 
them

explanation:
Without change-request knowledge, out-of-scope work gets done and in-scope features 
are delayed or defective.

question: Why is a vigorous defect reduction process still necessary?

options.D: Realistically, defects will exist no matter how good defect prevention is

explanation:
Even with good prevention, defects will exist, so a vigorous reduction process is still 
needed.

question: Inspection is best described as:

options.A: A walkthrough of different artifacts to provide another "eye" for finding defects

explanation:
Inspections are walkthroughs of artifacts, code included, that give another pair of eyes to 
spot problems.

question: In the inspection example, what caused the normal login to break?

options.B:
The social media login plugin was changing a variable status at the database level used by the 
normal login; a different plugin was chosen

explanation:
The social media plugin changed a database variable used by normal login, so a different 
plugin was chosen.

question: Testing is defined as a core Quality Assurance activity where the Quality Assurance team:

options.C: Executes the product to find defects and ensure it gives the required output

explanation:
Testing executes the product to find defects and confirm the required output, starting 
formally when code is handed to Quality Assurance.

question: Defect containment is most important for high-impact applications such as:
explanation: In medical, transportation and nuclear software, the risks of defects are very high.

question: Because exhaustive testing is impossible, the final possible strategy is to:

options.D: Break the fault-failure relation to contain the damage

explanation:
Since testing every condition is impossible, the final strategy is to break the fault-failure 
relation to contain the damage.

question:
Which statement correctly describes the tension between customer and developer quality 
requirements, as presented in Lecture 1?

options.A:
Customers prioritise qualities such as maintainability and reusability, whereas developers 
prioritise qualities such as efficiency and reliability.
options.B:
Customers and developers hold the same quality requirements but express them in 
different terminology.
options.C:
Customers stress efficiency and reliability, whereas developers stress maintainability and 
reusability.
options.D:
Customers emphasise qualities that can be specified unambiguously, whereas developers 
emphasise qualities that cannot be specified.

explanation:
Source: lec_1.pptx, Slide 3 
A. Incorrect. Reversed: efficiency and reliability are the customer's requirements, maintainability and reusability 
the developer's. 
B. Incorrect. The slide describes a genuine tension between different requirements, not a terminology 
difference. 
C. Correct. Matches Slide 3 exactly. 
D. Incorrect. Slide 3 says some quality requirements are hard to specify, but does not divide them between 
customer and developer this way.

question:
A developer misreads the requirement to add two numbers and writes the statement ans = value1 - 
value2. When the program runs, it displays a wrong result. Using the terminology of Module 1, 
which sequence correctly names the developer's mistake, the incorrect statement, and the wrong 
output, in order of occurrence?
explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, sections J–M (Fault, Failure and their examples) and D (Error) 
A. Correct. Error (human mistake) leads to a fault (incorrect step in the program), which leads to a failure (wrong 
behaviour). 
B. Incorrect. Reverses the first two: faults are the result of errors, not the cause of them. 
C. Incorrect. Reverses the whole chain; failure is the result of a fault. 
D. Incorrect. Failure is the result of a fault, so it cannot come before the fault.

question:
A project has a fixed, closed budget of PKR 100,000 for four features, with PKR 80,000 for 
development and PKR 20,000 for quality activities. The client then requests additional features at 
the same total price. According to Module 02, what is the most likely consequence?

options.A:
The quality allocation increases, because each additional feature requires more verification 
effort.
options.B:
The quality allocation is unaffected, because quality is budgeted separately from the 
features that are added.
options.C:
The total budget expands automatically so that functionality and quality can both be 
funded.
options.D:
The share of the fixed budget left for quality activities shrinks, so product quality tends to 
decrease.

explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, sections B–C (Function-Quality-Cost; Quality vs. Pre-defined Budget) 
A. Incorrect. The module says more features reduce the budget share for quality. 
B. Incorrect. Features and quality compete for the same fixed budget, so they are not independent. 
C. Incorrect. The budget is closed and fixed in this scenario; it does not expand. 
D. Correct. Matches the module: in a closed-budget project, more features mean lower quality.

question:
Defects keep recurring in a project because project managers do not know how to handle change 
requests. The organisation trains its managers in the change-request process so that this source of 
defects stops arising. Under the QA classification scheme in the notes, this response is mainly:

options.A: defect detection, because it finds defects that have already been injected.
options.B: defect prevention, because it addresses a root cause so that the defects do not recur.
options.C: defect containment, because it limits the damage caused by escaping defects.
options.D:
post-release defect repair, because the defects were found in versions that had already 
been released.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, sections B, G, L, M 
A. Incorrect. Detection finds existing defects; this response targets their cause. 
B. Correct. Correct: prevention addresses root causes to avoid future occurrence. 
C. Incorrect. Containment limits damage from defects that already exist; it does not remove their cause. 
D. Incorrect. Post-release repair is not a QA category in the scheme and the response does not repair defects.

question:
A hospital deploys a system that satisfies every requirement in its specification. Staff nevertheless 
find it unsuitable for the conditions on the ward where it is used. Which statement best describes 
this outcome in terms of the quality types in Lecture 2?

options.A:
Product quality is low, because meeting the specification alone does not make a product fit 
for its intended purpose.
options.B:
Process quality is low, because an unfit product implies that the defined processes were not 
completed.
options.C:
Product quality and quality in use are both satisfied, because the specification defines 
fitness for purpose.
options.D:
Product quality is satisfied, but quality in use is not, because fitness for purpose depends 
on the context of use.

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 2 
A. Incorrect. Lecture 2 defines product quality as the degree to which requirements are met, which holds here. 
B. Incorrect. The stem gives no information about the process; the inference is unsupported. 
C. Incorrect. Quality in use concerns fitness in a particular context, which the staff say is not met. 
D. Correct. Matches the definitions of product quality and quality in use.

question:
A risk analyst estimates that a quality failure has a probability of 0.05 and would cause a potential 
loss of PKR 2,000,000. Using the relationship given in Module 02, the risk exposure is:
explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, section J (Risk Analysis Approach) 
A. Incorrect. Not obtainable from RE = P × L with these values. 
B. Correct. Correct: 0.05 × 2,000,000 = 100,000. 
C. Incorrect. This is the potential loss, not the exposure; probability is ignored. 
D. Incorrect. Obtained by dividing the loss by the probability, which is not the stated relationship.

question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a bug from a defect, as these terms are used in Module 1?

options.A:
A bug is an error found before the software is shipped, whereas a defect is a deviation 
from customer requirements, mostly found after shipment.
options.B:
A bug is a deviation from customer requirements found at the production site, whereas a 
defect is an error found and accepted by developers before shipment.
options.C:
A bug is a human action that produces an incorrect result, whereas a defect is the inability 
of a program to behave as expected.
options.D:
A bug can be eliminated by effective defect prevention, whereas a defect is unavoidable 
once the software has been shipped.

explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, sections F and H (Defect, Bug) 
A. Correct. Matches Module 1's definitions. 
B. Incorrect. Swaps the two definitions. 
C. Incorrect. These are the definitions of an error and a failure, not of a bug and a defect. 
D. Incorrect. Module 1 states there is no bug-free software, so bugs cannot be eliminated by prevention alone.

question:
A report-generation module produces correct totals for every test input, but takes about three 
minutes to produce a report where the specification requires a response within ten seconds. Using 
the quality types in Lecture 1, which assessment is most accurate?

options.A:
Functional quality is deficient, because the module does not do what it is supposed to do, 
since the report requirement is not being met.
options.B:
Latent quality is deficient, because the module is slow at present and is therefore expected 
to remain slow.
options.C:
Functional quality is satisfactory, but non-functional quality is deficient, since the module 
works less well than required.
options.D:
Non-functional quality is satisfactory, because correct results matter more than the time 
taken to produce them.

explanation:
Source: lec_1.pptx, Slide 6 
A. Incorrect. The totals are correct, so what the module does matches what it should do. 
B. Incorrect. Latent quality concerns how well the software will continue to perform in future; the stem concerns 
current performance against a stated requirement. 
C. Correct. Functional quality is what the software does; non-functional quality is how well it does it. 
D. Incorrect. Non-functional quality compares how well it works with how well it should; the ten-second 
requirement is not met.

question:
A supermarket's cash register handles thousands of purchases of bread, milk and cheese every day 
without problems. The whole system freezes when a customer pays with cash, a credit card and a 
gift voucher together. Which explanation best fits the notes' account of such pre-release defects?

options.A:
The defect lay in the most heavily used scanning function, which had received the most QA 
attention.
options.B:
The defect was a known bug that the developers had accepted and deliberately shipped 
with the release.
options.C:
The defect arose because the developers lacked adequate knowledge of the terminology 
used in retail work.
options.D:
It stayed dormant in a rarely exercised area with little QA focus and was triggered only by 
an unusual situation.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, sections C–D (Pre-Release Defects, cash register example) 
A. Incorrect. The scanning function works without trouble, so the defect is not there. 
B. Incorrect. Nothing indicates the bug was known; the notes say the payment method was not tested properly. 
C. Incorrect. Domain knowledge is not the cause given in this example. 
D. Correct. Matches the notes: dormant defects sit in low-priority areas and are triggered by specific situations.

question:
The tree-swing illustration in Lecture 2 shows six panels, from "As Management Requested It" to 
"What The User Wanted". Which conclusion is best supported by the illustration?

options.A:
The product delivered can differ markedly from what the user wanted, because 
requirements are reinterpreted at each stage.
options.B:
The programmers' version is the closest to what the user wanted, so errors arise mainly 
during the design stage.
options.C:
Management's request and the user's need are identical, so any deviation from the user's 
need arises only after installation.
options.D:
Only the installed version differs from what the user needed, since all the earlier panels 
show the same design.

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 3 (Different Views of Quality, tree-swing illustration) 
A. Correct. Panels 1 to 5 each differ from one another and from panel 6. 
B. Incorrect. The programmers' panel does not resemble the user's need, so it cannot be the closest. 
C. Incorrect. Panel 1 and panel 6 differ visibly. 
D. Incorrect. The earlier panels show different designs from each other.

question:
Years after a serious software failure, a company finds that investors have steadily withdrawn their 
trust and that its market share has eroded, although no single loss was visible at the time of the 
incident. Under the Eppler and Helfert classification in Module 02, these losses are best described 
as:

options.A: direct costs, because loss of investment is a financial loss that can be measured at the time.
options.B:
indirect costs, because they are hidden, hard to calculate and emerge long after the 
incident.
options.C:
direct costs, because they originate from the missing quality in the software that was 
delivered.
options.D: indirect costs, because they are observed immediately but cannot be expressed in money.

explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, sections G–H (Direct and Indirect Cost of missing Quality) 
A. Incorrect. Financial loss is a direct-cost example, but loss of investor trust and market share is listed as 
indirect, being delayed and hard to measure. 
B. Correct. Matches the module's description of indirect costs. 
C. Incorrect. Both direct and indirect costs are linked to missing quality; origin does not separate them. 
D. Incorrect. Indirect costs are not observed immediately; they appear after a long time.

question:
Two builds of an application provide the same required functions at the same level of performance 
under the same stated conditions. Build X uses noticeably less memory, disk space and network 
capacity than Build Y. Which ISO-9126 characteristic distinguishes the two builds?
explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, ISO-9126: Efficiency 
A. Incorrect. Both builds provide the same functions. 
B. Incorrect. Both maintain the same performance level under the same conditions. 
C. Correct. Efficiency relates performance to the resources used. 
D. Incorrect. Portability concerns transfer between environments, which is not at issue.

question:
A vendor discovers a defect in a product that is already installed at many customer sites. Which 
statement best explains why this post-release defect is typically more costly to the vendor than one 
found before release?

options.A:
Post-release defects are technically more complex because they involve more modules than 
defects found earlier.
options.B:
The customers must bear the cost of repair, which raises the compensation payments the 
vendor has to make.
options.C:
Testing at the production site is inherently more expensive than inspection carried out 
during development.
options.D:
The fix must be applied at every installation, and the vendor's reputation, trust and 
market position suffer.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, section E (Post-Release Defects) 
A. Incorrect. Complexity is not the reason the notes give. 
B. Incorrect. The notes say the supplier pays to fix post-release defects. 
C. Incorrect. The notes do not compare testing and inspection costs. 
D. Correct. Matches the notes: multiple installations plus damage to image and market position.

question:
Which pair of models does Lecture 2 classify as application or company specific, rather than 
standard?
explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 4 (Quality Models) 
A. Correct. Both are listed under application or company specific models. 
B. Incorrect. Both are standard models. 
C. Incorrect. ISO/IEC 9126 is a standard model. 
D. Incorrect. McCall is a standard model.

question:
A project team cannot predict when or where a quality failure might occur in its software. Why does 
Module 02 regard risk analysis as a better way to evaluate the cost of missing quality in this 
situation?

options.A:
It records the actual losses after every failure, so the cost can be summed once the events 
are known.
options.B:
It removes the probability of failure by identifying and fixing the root cause of each possible 
event.
options.C:
It estimates cost from probability and potential loss, so the time and place of an event 
need not be known.
options.D:
It classifies costs as direct or indirect, so that only the visible and measurable losses need to 
be estimated.

explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, section J (Risk Analysis Approach) 
A. Incorrect. That describes measuring costs after the fact, not risk analysis. 
B. Incorrect. Root-cause analysis belongs to the impact analysis approach and does not remove probability. 
C. Correct. Matches the module: risk exposure combines probability and potential loss. 
D. Incorrect. Direct and indirect classification is a separate approach, and indirect costs would be ignored.

question:
During an acceptance review, evaluators confirm that a system performs its required functions and 
meets its performance targets today. They then ask how well it can be expected to continue 
performing in the future. Which quality type from Lecture 1 does this last question address?
explanation:
Source: lec_1.pptx, Slide 6 
A. Incorrect. Functional quality concerns what the software does versus what it should do. 
B. Correct. Latent quality is how well the software will continue to do it in the future. 
C. Incorrect. Non-functional quality concerns how well it does it now versus how well it should. 
D. Incorrect. Quality in use concerns fitness for purpose in a particular context of use, not future performance.

question:
A company acquires a software system for its employees to use. Compared with the employees who 
use the system, which additional concern is characteristic of the acquiring customer, according to 
Module 1?

options.A: The cost of the software solution
options.B: Fulfilling contractual obligations by delivering a product that conforms to its specifications
options.C: The choice of programming languages and development tools
options.D: The ease with which the code can be modified by the maintenance team

explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, Roles and Responsibility (Consumer: Users and Customer) 
A. Correct. Customers share users' expectations with additional concentration on cost. 
B. Incorrect. This is the producer's biggest concern. 
C. Incorrect. Choice of languages and tools is associated with producers. 
D. Incorrect. Modifiability is listed among producer concerns.

question:
A defect escapes to customers after release, and the vendor must investigate and repair it at the 
customer sites. Which cost-of-quality category in Lecture 2 does this repair effort belong to?
explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 5 (Cost of Quality) 
A. Incorrect. Prevention cost is spent to stop defects arising, not to repair them. 
B. Incorrect. Appraisal cost relates to checking the product, not repairing escaped defects. 
C. Incorrect. Internal failure cost is incurred before the product reaches customers. 
D. Correct. The defect reached customers, so this is an external failure.

question:
A log-export feature was tested with 30,000 records and worked correctly. In production, records 
went missing from the CSV file beyond 500,000 records. The SRS stated no upper limit on record 
volume. What does this case most directly show?

options.A:
The export logic was never tested before release, so the defect could not have been 
detected in advance.
options.B:
A plugin that changed database variables used by another module caused the missing 
records.
options.C:
A gap in the requirements kept the test volume far below production volume, so the 
defect appeared after release.
options.D:
The production site changed the requirement after delivery, which then caused the records 
to go missing.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, section F (Example of Post-Release Defects) 
A. Incorrect. The feature was tested, with 30,000 records. 
B. Incorrect. That is the cause in the login inspection example, not this one. 
C. Correct. Matches the example: no upper limit in the SRS led to a test volume of 30,000 against failures beyond 
500,000. 
D. Incorrect. Nothing says the requirement changed.

question:
A product has an excellent user interface but no firewall protecting its database. With additional 
money available for quality, which use does Module 02 support in order to lower the probability of 
product failure?

options.A:
Further cosmetic improvements to the interface, because users tend to judge a product by 
its appearance first.
options.B:
Adding the database firewall, because missing protection leaves the product open to 
threats that UI polish cannot remove.
options.C:
Adding new features, because features determine the behaviour on which user satisfaction 
ultimately depends.
options.D:
Splitting the money equally between interface work and the firewall, because both 
contribute to overall quality.

explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, section D (What are Missing Quality Requirements?) 
A. Incorrect. The module says the firewall matters more than cosmetic UI changes. 
B. Correct. Matches the module's firewall versus cosmetic UI example. 
C. Incorrect. The money is for quality, and features compete with quality for budget. 
D. Incorrect. The module ranks the firewall above cosmetic changes rather than treating them equally.

question:
The Lecture 2 chart titled "Kill them before they cost you" shows the relative cost of fixing a 
software defect by life-cycle stage. Which statement is supported by the chart?

options.A:
Fixing a defect in customer testing costs more than in developer testing, and fixing it in 
service costs the most.
options.B:
Fixing a defect during developer testing costs more than fixing the same defect during 
customer testing.
options.C:
The cost of fixing a defect in service is roughly the same as the cost of fixing it in customer 
testing.
options.D:
The cost of fixing a defect falls once the software is released, because customers then report 
the faults.

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 5 (chart: Kill them before they cost you, Barry Boehm, TRW Inc.) 
A. Correct. Matches the chart: cost rises through developer testing, customer testing and in service. 
B. Incorrect. The customer testing bar is longer than the developer testing bar. 
C. Incorrect. The in-service bar is far longer than the customer testing bar. 
D. Incorrect. The in-service cost is the highest, not lower.

question:
In Module 1, the statement if ($Amount=100) is corrected to if ($Amount==100) and is presented as 
a semantic error. Which reason best explains this classification?

options.A:
The statement breaks the grammar of the language, so the program cannot be executed at 
all.
options.B: The statement calls a function that has not been defined anywhere in the program.
options.C:
The statement uses a variable name that differs from the name declared earlier in the 
program.
options.D:
The correction changes the logic of the condition, not the grammatical form of the 
statement.

explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, sections D–E (What is Error? / Example of Error) 
A. Incorrect. That would describe a syntax error; the source labels this one semantic and says the logic is 
changed. 
B. Incorrect. No undefined function is involved. 
C. Incorrect. The variable name is the same in both versions. 
D. Correct. Matches the source: the corrected version is annotated "Change the logic".

question:
Lecture 1 describes "quality means meeting the specification" as problematical for software 
systems. Which reason does the lecture give?

options.A: Software specifications are normally written only after the coding of the system is complete.
options.B:
Customers do not hold quality requirements for the software, so there is nothing for the 
specification to state.
options.C:
Specifications are usually incomplete and often inconsistent, and some quality 
requirements resist unambiguous statement.
options.D:
Conformance to a specification can be checked only after the software has been delivered 
to the customer.

explanation:
Source: lec_1.pptx, Slide 3 
A. Incorrect. Not stated in Lecture 1. 
B. Incorrect. The slide says customers do have quality requirements (efficiency, reliability, etc.). 
C. Correct. Matches the slide's stated reasons. 
D. Incorrect. Not stated in Lecture 1.

question:
In a shared code base, a code review discovered that the plugin used for social-media login was 
changing a database-level variable relied on by the normal login module, and the team replaced the 
plugin. Why do the notes describe inspection as direct fault detection and removal?

options.A:
The product is executed with chosen test inputs so that the resulting failures reveal where 
the faults lie.
options.B:
The review removes the source of errors from the development process so that defects are 
not injected later.
options.C: The review limits the damage when a fault is triggered by breaking the fault-failure relation.
options.D:
Human inspectors examine the artifact itself, so existing defects are typically located 
precisely and fixed easily.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, sections O–P (Inspection) 
A. Incorrect. That describes testing, not inspection. 
B. Incorrect. That describes defect prevention. 
C. Incorrect. That describes defect containment. 
D. Correct. Matches the quotation from Tian in the notes.

question:
Which pairing of activity and category is consistent with the classification scheme for QA in Lecture 
2?

options.A: Process conformance and standards enforcement: defect prevention
options.B: Static testing of documents and code: defect containment
options.C: Software fault tolerance: defect reduction (detection and removal)
options.D: Education and training of the team: defect containment

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 8 (Classification scheme for QA) 
A. Correct. Listed under defect prevention. 
B. Incorrect. Static testing is listed under defect reduction. 
C. Incorrect. Software fault tolerance is listed under defect containment. 
D. Incorrect. Education and training is listed under defect prevention.

question:
A software system is used continuously, with interruptions only for version changes. Its failure could 
seriously threaten human lives, cause permanent injury or severe illness, and damage the 
environment, with important economic or social impact. Which IEEE criticality level in Module 02 
matches this description?
explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, section K (Level of Risk) 
A. Incorrect. Level A involves 24-hour usage, irreversible environmental damage and loss of human lives. 
B. Correct. Matches the Level B descriptors. 
C. Incorrect. Level C involves property damage and minor injury or illness. 
D. Incorrect. Level D involves no risk to human lives.

question:
A team plans to add a ready-made plugin to its application. Which statement from Module 1 best 
justifies analysing the plugin carefully before adopting it?

options.A:
Off-the-shelf products always cost less than developing the same functionality inside the 
organisation.
options.B:
Off-the-shelf products must be developed and tested together with the solution that will 
use them.
options.C:
Off-the-shelf products are developed and tested independently, and one solution does not 
fit all.
options.D: Off-the-shelf products are available only to users who are willing to pay for them.

explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, Off the Shelf Products 
A. Incorrect. Cost advantage is not claimed. 
B. Incorrect. They are developed and tested independently. 
C. Correct. Matches the Module 1 text on OTS products. 
D. Incorrect. OTS products are available at cost or not.

question:
An audit finds that several planned review and approval steps in an organisation's defined process 
were skipped, although the delivered software passes all its requirement-based acceptance tests. 
Which statement is most accurate according to Lecture 2?

options.A:
Process quality is deficient, because it is the degree to which the defined processes were 
followed and completed.
options.B:
Product quality is deficient, because skipped steps necessarily lower the degree to which 
requirements are met.
options.C:
Quality in use is deficient, because skipped steps mean the software cannot be fit for its 
purpose.
options.D:
Neither is deficient, because process quality is determined solely by whether the product 
meets its requirements.

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 2 
A. Correct. Matches the definition of process quality. 
B. Incorrect. Product quality is the degree to which requirements are met, which the tests show is satisfied. 
C. Incorrect. Nothing is said about the context of use. 
D. Incorrect. Process quality is about following defined processes, not about product requirements.

question:
A team building medical software has applied training, reviews and extensive testing. It accepts that 
testing cannot cover every condition and that some faults may still be triggered in rare situations. 
According to the notes, which strategy addresses this remaining risk?

options.A:
Continue testing until every possible condition and every combination of inputs has been 
executed.
options.B:
Strengthen education and training so that no faults can be injected into the software in 
future.
options.C:
Increase the number of inspections so that all remaining faults are removed before the 
release.
options.D:
Break the relation between faults and failures so that triggered faults do not cause 
damage.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, section R (Defect Containment) 
A. Incorrect. The notes say exhaustive testing is impossible. 
B. Incorrect. Prevention cannot guarantee a defect-free product. 
C. Incorrect. Reduction cannot remove all faults. 
D. Correct. Matches the notes: the final strategy is to break the fault-failure relation to contain damage.

question:
In the Yahoo breach discussed in Module 02, which option correctly pairs each party with 
consequences the module identifies?

options.A:
Customers: lawsuits and the cost of investigating the root cause. Yahoo: loss of privacy and 
confidential information.
options.B:
Customers: loss of privacy and confidential information. Yahoo: loss of trust, financial loss, 
lawsuits, investigation costs.
options.C:
Customers: no consequences, because the breach was a supplier-side event. Yahoo: all of 
the consequences.
options.D: Customers: physical injury. Yahoo: loss of market share, with no other consequences.

explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, sections E and I (Cost of Missing Quality Requirements; Impact Analysis 
Approach) 
A. Incorrect. Swaps the parties. 
B. Correct. Matches section I. 
C. Incorrect. The module says both customers and suppliers bear consequences. 
D. Incorrect. Physical injury is not reported for Yahoo, and Yahoo's consequences are wider.

question: Which statement best reflects the definition of software quality assurance given in Lecture 2?

options.A:
Testing carried out by the QA team after the code is handed over, to prove that the software 
has no defects.
options.B:
Reactive work performed after a failure is reported, to restore the level of quality that was 
required.
options.C:
Planned and systematic activities within a quality system that give adequate confidence 
that quality requirements will be met.
options.D:
Measures that guarantee an entity will be free of defects once all of its requirements have 
been met.

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 7 
A. Incorrect. The definition is not limited to testing and does not claim proof of zero defects. 
B. Incorrect. The definition describes planned activities, not reactive ones. 
C. Correct. Matches the quoted definition. 
D. Incorrect. The definition speaks of adequate confidence, not a guarantee.

question:
The defect-filtering figure in Module 1 passes customer requirements through four filters 
(requirement defects, design and planning defects, coding defects, testing defects) and ends with a 
"99.9% bug free product". Which conclusion is consistent with the figure and its accompanying text?

options.A:
Successive filters progressively reduce defects, yet even the final product cannot be called 
completely bug-free.
options.B: A single filter at the testing stage is sufficient to remove all of the defects introduced earlier.
options.C:
The filters are applied in the order testing, coding, design and requirements, so the latest 
defects are removed first.
options.D:
Once the requirements filter has been applied, no further defect can be injected at any later 
stage.

explanation:
Source: SQE_Discipline.pdf, Defect Prevention (figure) and Defect Detection or Reduction 
A. Correct. Matches the figure and text: 99.99% does not mean 100%. 
B. Incorrect. Four filters are shown and the product still falls short of 100%. 
C. Incorrect. The figure places requirements first and testing last. 
D. Incorrect. The figure shows defects at the design, coding and testing stages too.

question:
A team is developing a property-tax calculation system in which rates depend on property category, 
covered area and the applicable law. The developers are purely technical resources. Why do the 
notes suggest involving a domain specialist?

options.A: To write the code faster, since domain specialists are more productive than the developers.
options.B: To replace the business analysts, who are unable to interpret the terms used in the domain.
options.C:
To remove the need for written requirements, since specialists already know what has to be 
built.
options.D:
To make sure domain terminology and rules are interpreted correctly, since weak domain 
knowledge causes ambiguity and confusion.

explanation:
Source: Quality_Assurance_Basics.pdf, sections I–J (Domain Knowledge) 
A. Incorrect. Productivity is not the stated reason. 
B. Incorrect. Specialists work with business analysts and/or developers; they do not replace them. 
C. Incorrect. Requirements remain necessary. 
D. Correct. Matches the notes.

question:
According to Lecture 2, what role does the SQA plan play when the quality measured during 
development falls outside the planned quality levels?

options.A:
It automatically halts development until the planned levels of quality have been re-
established.
options.B:
It provides the basis for comparing actual and planned quality and documents 
management's response.
options.C:
It transfers responsibility for corrective action from management to the independent test 
observer.
options.D:
It replaces the planned levels with the lower levels that were actually achieved during 
development.

explanation:
Source: lec_2.pptx, Slide 11 (SQA Plan) 
A. Incorrect. The slide does not say development is halted automatically. 
B. Correct. Matches Slide 11. 
C. Incorrect. The slide says management responds as documented in the plan. 
D. Incorrect. Nothing says planned levels are lowered.

question:
Module 02 links user satisfaction to requirements through a chain of facts. Which conclusion follows 
from that chain when the quality requirements of a product are missing?

options.A:
User satisfaction is unaffected, because satisfaction depends only on the features that have 
been implemented.
options.B:
User satisfaction is unaffected, because behaviour is defined by the code rather than by the 
requirements.
options.C:
Those qualities are not built into the code's behaviour, weakening overall behaviour and 
user satisfaction.
options.D:
The code will implement the missing qualities automatically, since behaviour is realised 
through code.

explanation:
Source: Cost_of_Software_Quality.pdf, section A (Economics of Software Quality Engineering) 
A. Incorrect. The module says behaviour is defined through features and quality. 
B. Incorrect. The module says features and quality are determined through requirements. 
C. Correct. Follows the chain: requirements determine features and quality, code executes behaviour, behaviour 
drives satisfaction. 
D. Incorrect. Code implements only what the requirements specify.
